learn.hook: 2 samosas and 3 jalebis cost ₹110. How much is one samosa? There isn't just one answer, until you get more clues!
points: A linear equation in two variables can be written as ax + by + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a and b are not both zero.
A solution is an ordered pair (x, y) that makes the equation true. Example: (2, 3) is a solution of 2x + y = 7 because 4 + 3 = 7.
A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions: choose any x, then work out y.
To check a pair, substitute both values and see whether the two sides are equal.
An equation like y = 3 can be written in two variables as 0·x + 1·y − 3 = 0.
learn.reallife: Shopkeepers mixing two kinds of sweets in a ₹500 box face a two-variable equation: many different mixes give the same total.

games.title: Is it a solution of 2x + y = 7?

items.text: x + y = 10. If x = 4, then y = ___
x − y = 5. If y = 2, then x = ___
A linear equation in two variables has ___ solutions

quiz.q: Which ordered pair is a solution of 2x + y = 7?
quiz.mistake: Swaps x and y in the ordered pair

quiz.q: A pen costs ₹x and a notebook costs ₹y. 2 pens and 3 notebooks cost ₹110. Which equation shows this?
quiz.explain: Cost of 2 pens = 2x and of 3 notebooks = 3y. Together: 2x + 3y = 110.
quiz.mistake: Attaches the numbers to the wrong items

quiz.q: If (k, 2) is a solution of 3x − 2y = 8, what is k?
quiz.explain: Substitute x = k, y = 2: 3k − 4 = 8, so 3k = 12 and k = 4.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 4 instead of adding it, getting 4/3

quiz.q: How many solutions does x + y = 10 have?
quiz.explain: For every value of x there is a matching y = 10 − x, such as (1, 9), (2.5, 7.5), (−3, 13), and so on.
quiz.mistake: Counts only whole-number solutions, or treats it like a one-variable equation

quiz.q: Write 4x − 5y + 6 = 0 in the form ax + by + c = 0. What is b?
quiz.explain: Compare term by term: a = 4, b = −5, c = 6. The sign belongs to the coefficient.
quiz.mistake: Drops the minus sign in front of 5y

quiz.q: For x + 2y = 12, find y when x = 4.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide by 2, giving y = 8

quiz.q: How can y = 3 be written as a linear equation in two variables?
quiz.explain: The coefficient of x is 0, so x can take any value while y stays 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks an equation without x cannot have two variables

quiz.q: A box holds 60 sweets: x laddoos and y pedas. Which equation describes the box?
quiz.explain: The numbers of laddoos and pedas together make 60.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the two amounts instead of adding them

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "For x + y = 5, my friend says the answer is (2, 3) and I say (1, 4). Who is right?"
teach.praise: You are both right! Put each pair in and the sum is 5. A two-variable equation has infinitely many solutions. Happy chirps!
teach.nudge: What happens when you put (2, 3) and (1, 4) into x + y? Can an equation like this have more than one answer?

learn.hook: Plot every solution of x + y = 5 and they line up perfectly, like students at assembly. One equation, one straight line!
points: The graph of a linear equation in two variables is a straight line. Every point on the line is a solution, and every solution is a point on the line.
To draw it, find two or three solutions, plot them and join them with a ruler.
x-intercept: put y = 0. y-intercept: put x = 0. These two points are often the easiest to plot.
x = a is a vertical line through (a, 0); y = b is a horizontal line through (0, b).
y = mx (with no constant term) always passes through the origin (0, 0).

steps: Plot the three points and join them: one straight line

learn.reallife: A taxi fare chart (fare against distance) or a mobile recharge plan (cost against data) shows up as a straight-line graph.

games.title: Line logic
items: Every point on the graph of 2x + y = 6 is a solution of the equation
The line is made of exactly the solutions.
The graph of x = 5 is a horizontal line
x stays 5 while y changes, so the line is vertical.
The point (2, 1) lies on x + y = 4
Two points are enough to draw the graph of a linear equation
Exactly one straight line passes through two points.

quiz.q: What does the graph of x = 4 look like?
quiz.explain: Every point has x = 4 and any y, so the points form a vertical line crossing the x-axis at (4, 0).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up vertical and horizontal lines

quiz.q: Where does the line 2x + 3y = 12 cut the x-axis?
quiz.explain: On the x-axis y = 0, so 2x = 12 and x = 6. The point is (6, 0).
quiz.mistake: Puts x = 0 instead of y = 0, which gives the y-axis point

quiz.q: Where does the line 2x + 3y = 12 cut the y-axis?
quiz.explain: On the y-axis x = 0, so 3y = 12 and y = 4. The point is (0, 4).
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide 12 by the coefficient of y

quiz.q: Which line passes through the origin?
quiz.explain: Put x = 0 in y = 5x: y = 0, so (0, 0) is on the line. The others do not contain (0, 0).
quiz.mistake: Thinks every line passes through the origin

quiz.q: The point (2, k) lies on the line y = 3x − 1. What is k?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract 1, or adds it

quiz.q: What does the graph of y = −2 look like?
options: A vertical line left of the y-axis
A horizontal line 2 units below the x-axis
A horizontal line 2 units above the x-axis
quiz.explain: Every point has y = −2, so the line is horizontal and lies 2 units below the x-axis.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the minus sign

quiz.q: Where do the lines x = 3 and y = −1 meet?
quiz.explain: The meeting point must have x = 3 and y = −1, so it is (3, −1).
quiz.mistake: Writes the coordinates in the wrong order

quiz.q: The line x + y = 6 makes a triangle with the two axes. What is the area of this triangle?
quiz.explain: The line meets the axes at (6, 0) and (0, 6). The triangle has base 6 and height 6, so area = ½ × 6 × 6 = 18.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ½ in the triangle formula

teach.ask: Gappu has graph paper: "How do I draw the graph of x + y = 4? Do I need lots of points?"
teach.praise: Find two or three solutions like (0, 4), (4, 0) and (2, 2), plot them, and join them with a ruler into a straight line!
teach.nudge: Which pairs (x, y) make x + y = 4 true? What do you do once they are plotted?

learn.hook: One clue gives infinitely many answers. Add a second clue and, usually, just one answer is left. Two lines, one meeting point!
points: Two linear equations in the same two variables form a pair. A solution of the pair must satisfy both equations.
Graphically, the solution is the point where the two lines meet.
Lines that cross give exactly one solution. Parallel lines give no solution. Lines that lie on top of each other (the same line) give infinitely many solutions.
Substitution method: make one variable the subject in one equation and put it into the other.
Elimination method: add or subtract the equations (after multiplying if needed) to remove one variable.

example.q: Solve x + y = 10 and x − y = 2.
steps: Put x = 6 in x + y = 10: y = 4

learn.reallife: Comparing two mobile plans, or finding prices from two shopping bills, is solving a pair of linear equations.

items.q: x + y = 8, x − y = 2. Find x.
x + y = 8, x − y = 2. Find y.

quiz.q: Solve x + y = 12 and x − y = 4.
quiz.explain: Adding gives 2x = 16, so x = 8; then y = 12 − 8 = 4. Check: 8 − 4 = 4 ✓.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the values of x and y

quiz.q: 2 pens and 1 notebook cost ₹50. 1 pen and 1 notebook cost ₹35. What is the cost of one pen?
quiz.explain: Subtract the second bill from the first: the extra pen costs 50 − 35 = ₹15.
quiz.mistake: Gives the notebook's price (₹20) instead of the pen's

quiz.q: How many solutions does the pair y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3 have?
quiz.explain: Both lines have slope 2 but different y-intercepts, so they are parallel and never meet.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every pair of lines must cross somewhere

quiz.q: How many solutions does the pair x + 2y = 4 and 2x + 4y = 8 have?
quiz.explain: The second equation is just the first multiplied by 2, so both describe the same line. Every point on it is a solution.
quiz.mistake: Thinks different-looking equations must be different lines

quiz.q: Solve y = 3x and x + y = 20. What is y?
quiz.explain: Substitute y = 3x: x + 3x = 20, so 4x = 20, x = 5 and y = 15.
quiz.mistake: Gives the value of x (5) instead of y

quiz.q: Kabir is 4 years older than Aisha. The sum of their ages is 30. How old is Aisha?
quiz.explain: Let Aisha be a and Kabir k: k = a + 4 and a + k = 30. So 2a + 4 = 30, a = 13 and Kabir is 17.
quiz.mistake: Gives Kabir's age (17) or just halves 30

quiz.q: On a graph, how do you read off the solution of a pair of linear equations?
options: Where each line cuts the y-axis
The point where the two lines meet
Where each line cuts the x-axis
quiz.explain: Only the meeting point lies on both lines, so only it satisfies both equations.
quiz.mistake: Reads the intercepts of one line instead of the common point

quiz.q: At a zoo, adult tickets cost ₹60 and child tickets ₹40. A group buys 10 tickets for ₹480. How many adult tickets did they buy?
quiz.explain: Let a adults and c children: a + c = 10 and 60a + 40c = 480. Then 60a + 40(10 − a) = 480, so 20a = 80 and a = 4.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of child tickets (6)

teach.ask: Gappu draws two lines on a graph: "Where is the answer to both equations together?"
teach.praise: The answer is where the two lines meet, because that point is on both. Parallel lines never meet, so then there is no solution. Super!
teach.nudge: Which point is on both lines at once? And what if the lines never meet?
